# Postmortem: API Latency Spike on checkout-service — 2025-08-18 (INC-1427)
- Status: Resolved
- Severity: SEV-2
- Impact: ~31% of checkout requests experienced p95 latency > 5s; 2.1% error rate; estimated revenue impact ≈ $38k
- Start: 2025-08-18 14:07 UTC
- End: 2025-08-18 14:52 UTC
- Duration: 45m

## Summary
At 14:07 UTC, traffic was shifted to checkout-service v3.2.1 as part of a blue/green cutover. A misconfigured Envoy global rate limit filter unintentionally throttled critical checkout routes, causing request queuing, elevated latency, and intermittent 429/5xx errors. Rollback to v3.1.8 at 14:18 UTC restored capacity; full recovery confirmed at 14:52 UTC.

## Timeline
- 14:07 — Blue/green cutover to v3.2.1 initiated via ArgoCD
- 14:10 — p95 latency climbs above 2s
- 14:12 — PagerDuty alert triggered (SLO-CHK-P95>2s) for checkout-service
- 14:16 — Incident declared (INC-1427); comms opened in Slack #inc-1427
- 14:18 — Rollback to v3.1.8 started
- 14:23 — Latency and errors trending down; partial recovery
- 14:52 — Metrics back to baseline; incident resolved

## Root Cause
A values.yaml change enabled a global rate limit with a default domain and a low threshold intended only for canary tests. When the cutover completed, the limit applied to all checkout routes, producing throttling and backpressure.

## Contributing Factors
- Lack of guardrails preventing global limits in production defaults
- Canary validation did not include sustained load at peak checkout traffic
- Alerting covered latency but not explicit 429 rate spikes on critical routes

## Detection and Response
- Detection: Prometheus alert SLO-CHK-P95>2s, Grafana dashboard anomalies
- On-call: @maria (app), escalated to @rahul (platform) and @lena (networking)
- Comms: Slack #inc-1427; Statuspage updates every 10 minutes

## Metrics
| Metric              | Baseline | Incident Peak |
|---------------------|----------|---------------|
| API p95 latency     | 350 ms   | 6200 ms       |
| HTTP 5xx            | 0.2%     | 2.1%          |
| HTTP 429            | ~0%      | 4.8%          |
| Checkouts/min       | 4,200    | 2,900         |

## Relevant Config (problematic)
```yaml
rate_limit:
  enabled: true
  domain: global
  descriptors:
    - key: route
      value: checkout
      rate_limit:
        unit: second
        requests_per_unit: 50
```

| Add canary integration test for rate-limit behaviors     | Maria  | SRE-874     | P1       | 2025-08-25 |

| Update checkout-service runbook with rollback checklist  | Lena   | SRE-875     | P2       | 2025-08-26 |

- ArgoCD app: https://argocd.company.io/applications/checkout-service

# Postmortem: API Gateway Outage — 2025-08-21
## Summary
Between 13:12–13:47 UTC on 2025-08-21, API Gateway v3 in us-east-1 returned elevated 502/503 responses due to misconfigured Network Load Balancer (NLB) target health checks after Terraform change TF-1042. During the incident, automated scaling and health check failures caused a subset of gateway targets to flap, leading to intermittent upstream errors.

## Impact
- Duration: 35 minutes (13:12–13:47 UTC)
- Affected region: us-east-1
- Error rate: Peaked at 23% 5xx
- Tenants impacted: 1,847
- Estimated financial credits: $18.7k

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Requests affected | ~3.2M (23%) |
| Peak concurrent errors | 12.4k/min |
| SLO error budget burned | 9.3% of monthly budget |
| Support tickets | 42 (SUP-9381 to SUP-9422) |

## Timeline
- 13:12 UTC — SLO breach alert fired (PagerDuty PD-INC-9482, “API v3 5xx > 5% for 5m”).
- 13:14 UTC — On-call acknowledged; traffic split verified; us-east-1 identified as hot region.
- 13:16 UTC — Grafana dashboard showed NLB target health flapping; error signatures 502/503 from upstream.
- 13:19 UTC — Change correlation found: Terraform apply (TF-1042) merged at 12:57 UTC modified NLB health_check_path from /health to /status.
- 13:25 UTC — Mitigation step: shifted 15% traffic to us-west-2 via weighted DNS; partial relief observed.
- 13:31 UTC — Rolled back NLB health check config to previous known-good (TF-1041) and forced target group refresh.
- 13:39 UTC — Target health stabilized; error rate trending down.
- 13:47 UTC — SLO alert cleared; traffic weights restored to baseline.

## Root Cause
A Terraform module upgrade (infra/modules/nlb v2.8.1 → v2.9.0) changed the default health_check_path from “/health” (200) to “/status” (returns 404 on API Gateway v3 pods without feature flag api_status_endpoint=true). This caused NLB to mark targets as unhealthy, triggering autoscaling replacements and connection churn. The change passed plan review but lacked an environment-specific validation of health endpoints.

## Detection
- Primary: SLO-based alert (5xx > 5% for 5m) via Prometheus Alertmanager → PagerDuty PD-INC-9482.
- Secondary: Synthetic canary checks failed in us-east-1 only (CheckID canary-apigw-v3-us-east-1).
- Customer reports started at 13:20 UTC (Zendesk).

## Resolution
- Reverted NLB health check path to “/health” using known-good state TF-1041 and re-applied to prod.
- Drained and re-registered targets to ensure stable health state.
- Temporarily shifted 15% traffic to us-west-2 to reduce error blast radius.
- Validated via Grafana (error rate <1% for 10m) and synthetic checks pass before closing.

## What Went Well
- SLO alerts triggered within 2 minutes of regression.
- Traffic shifting playbook executed smoothly with clear comms.

## What Didn’t Go Well
- Health-check endpoint drift between environments went unnoticed.
- Terraform module change lacked explicit health-check validation in CI for prod parity.

## Corrective Actions
- [ ] Pin nlb module to v2.8.x until parity tests exist (Owner: @alex.ng, Due: 2025-09-05)
- [ ] Add CI canary to validate health_check_path against live staging mirrors (Owner: @mei.chen, Due: 2025-09-10)
- [ ] Require “health-check verification” checklist item in infra PR template (Owner: @liam.parker, Due: 2025-09-03)
- [ ] Expand synthetic checks to validate /status and /health endpoints (Owner: @ops-analytics, Due: 2025-09-12)
- [ ] Update runbook: API Gateway v3 health endpoints and rollback steps (Owner: @sara.b, Due: 2025-09-06)

| Action | Owner | Due | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pin nlb module to v2.8.x | @alex.ng | 2025-09-05 | Open |
| Add CI canary health validation | @mei.chen | 2025-09-10 | Open |
| PR template checklist update | @liam.parker | 2025-09-03 | In Progress |
| Expand synthetic checks | @ops-analytics | 2025-09-12 | Open |
| Runbook update | @sara.b | 2025-09-06 | Open |

## Logs

2025-08-21T13:15:02Z nlb/target-group apigw-v3-tg healthcheck failed: GET /status -> 404
2025-08-21T13:16:11Z apigw-v3 pod-6d8b7f9dcd-2kx7z upstream error: 502 from auth-svc timeout=3s
2025-08-21T13:19:48Z terraform apply TF-1042 completed: updated target_group health_check { path=/status, interval=10s }
2025-08-21T13:31:56Z terraform apply TF-1041 completed: restored health_check { path=/health, interval=10s }

# Incident Postmortem: 2025-08-21 Checkout Latency (INC-3245)
- Authors: Alicia Park (@apark), Ravi Menon (@rmenon)
- Service: checkout-api (v3.18.2)
- Severity: SEV-2
- Start: 2025-08-21 14:07 UTC
- End: 2025-08-21 14:52 UTC
- Duration: 45m

## Summary
During a routine deploy of checkout-api v3.18.2, requests to /payments/authorize experienced p95 latency spikes from ~350ms to >5s, causing 3.8% checkout abandonment.

## Impact
- 28,416 impacted requests
- 1,127 failed authorizations (HTTP 504)
- Estimated revenue at risk: $84,500

## Timeline
| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 14:07 | Deploy started to us-east-1 canary |
| 14:12 | Alert fired: Checkout p95 > 2s |
| 14:20 | Rollout paused; error budget burn 3%/hr |

| 14:52 | Resolved; postmortem declared |

## Root Cause
A misconfigured connection pool in the new gRPC payments client set maxConcurrentStreams=100 (down from 1024), bottlenecking I/O under burst traffic; additionally, a Redis key eviction policy change increased cache misses for auth tokens.

## Detection
- Prometheus alert checkout_p95_latency_over_threshold

- [ ] Increase maxConcurrentStreams to 2048 and load test
- [ ] Revert Redis policy to allkeys-lru and add 20% capacity
- [ ] Add canary-specific load test in CI
- [ ] Create runbook for gRPC client tuning

- Jira: INC-3245, TECH-981

- gRPC client tune: @rmenon (due 2025-08-28)

## Summary

- Start: 2025-08-19 13:12 UTC
- End: 2025-08-19 13:47 UTC

- Affected Services: api-gateway, auth-service, redis-cache

## Timeline (UTC)
- 13:12 — PagerDuty alert fired (API p95 > 2s); on-call acknowledged (SRE: M. Chen)
- 13:15 — Noted spike in upstream auth-service 5xx and connection resets
- 13:21 — Rolled back api-gateway config from v2.4.1 to v2.4.0; partial improvement
- 13:28 — Increased auth-service pod count from 20 → 35; latency trending down
- 13:35 — Identified Envoy circuit breaker change in v2.4.1 limiting upstream connections
- 13:42 — Hotfix applied to restore previous thresholds; queues drained
- 13:47 — Latency and error rates returned to baseline; incident resolved

## Root Cause Analysis
A configuration regression in api-gateway (config v2.4.1) reduced the allowed upstream connections to auth-service, causing connection churn, elevated retries, and queuing under normal peak load. The change was introduced in a broader refactor of gateway defaults and bypassed the standard load test gate due to an incorrectly scoped canary.
```yaml
# Problematic (v2.4.1)
clusters:
  - name: auth_service
    circuit_breakers:
      thresholds:
        max_connections: 200
        max_pending_requests: 500

# Previous (v2.4.0)
clusters:
  - name: auth_service
    circuit_breakers:
      thresholds:
        max_connections: 2000
        max_pending_requests: 2000
```
Contributing factors:
- Canary scope excluded login-heavy traffic paths
- Alert for connection pool saturation not enabled on gateway tier
- Redis cache warmup coincided with traffic surge, amplifying auth load

## Mitigations & Corrective Actions
- [x] Roll back api-gateway to v2.4.0 (change 9e2f1c3)
- [x] Hotfix circuit breaker thresholds to previous safe values
- [ ] Add pre-merge load test for gateway defaults (SRE-912, Owner: M. Chen, Due: 2025-08-26)
- [ ] Reinstate canary on auth-heavy routes (PLAT-1203, Owner: L. Ortega, Due: 2025-08-28)

|-----------------------------|--------------------|-------------------|----------------|
| API Latency                 | 420 ms             | 2.8 s             | 430 ms         |
| Auth-service 5xx Rate       | 0.2%               | 4.7%              | 0.1%           |
| Gateway Retries per Request | 0.03               | 0.62              | 0.04           |

- External status page: Posted at 13:25 UTC, resolved at 13:50 UTC

## Links

- Logs (S3): s3://platform-logs/prod/api-gateway/2025/08/19/13/

- Establish explicit SLOs and alerts for connection pool saturation
- Automate rollback guardrails tied to latency SLO breaches

# Payments Service Runbook (v2, Aug 2025)
Last updated: 2025-08-22 by @dana.kim
Service: payments-api (Go 1.21) + payments-worker
Tier: 1
SLAs: 99.9% availability, P50 < 150ms, P95 < 500ms

Overview
The Payments Service handles card authorization, capture, and refunds for all checkout flows across web and mobile. Dependencies include: 3DS gateway (Adyen), Kafka topic payments.events.v3, Postgres cluster pg-payments-prod, and Secrets from Vault path secret/payments/prod.

Runbooks and Dashboards
- Grafana (Service Health): https://grafana.acme.internal/d/payments/overview
- Grafana (Kafka Lag): https://grafana.acme.internal/d/kafka/consumers?var=group=payments-worker
- Sentry: https://sentry.acme.internal/organizations/acme/projects/payments
- Kibana logs: https://kibana.acme.internal/app/discover#/payments
- PagerDuty service: ACME Payments (on-call)

On-call Checklist (at start of shift)
- Verify error budget burn: https://slo.acme.internal/services/payments
- Open #incidents-payments in Slack and set availability
- Acknowledge any pending PD alerts and review the last 24h in Sentry
- Confirm feature flags state in Flagr: payments.3ds_soft_failover, payments.idempotency_guard

Severity and Response Matrix
| Severity | Condition | First Response | Comms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SEV1 | Active outage, checkout failures > 5% | 5 min | Slack #incidents-payments, Statuspage (external) |
| SEV2 | Degraded, > 1% failures or P95 > 1s for 15m | 10 min | Slack #incidents-payments |
| SEV3 | Minor impact, single region or partial feature | 30 min | Slack #payments-eng |

Common Incidents and Playbooks

1) 3DS authorization failures > 2% (SEV1)
- Validate: Grafana “3DS Success Rate” panel; correlate with Adyen status page.
- Mitigate (soft failover):
  - Toggle feature flag to allow retry without 3DS when risk score < threshold.
  - Command:
    kubectl -n payments exec deploy/payments-api -- curl -s -XPOST http://flagr.flagr:18000/api/v1/flags/payments.3ds_soft_failover/enable
- Check Sentry for error key 3DS_AUTH_FAILED and capture rate by issuer BIN.
- If Adyen incident ongoing > 20 min, enable hard failover and update Statuspage.
- Post-incident: disable failover, reprocess stuck auths via replay job (see Job Replay section).

2) Kafka consumer lag > 50k on payments-worker (SEV2)
- Validate: Grafana “payments-worker Lag” panel and consumer group offsets.
- Scale workers:
  kubectl -n payments scale deploy/payments-worker --replicas=8
- If lag persists > 15m, check hot partitions and GC:
  kubectl -n payments top pods -l app=payments-worker
- If errors spike, pause retries:
  kubectl -n payments set env deploy/payments-worker RETRIES_ENABLED=false

3) DB failover or elevated write latency (SEV1)
- Validate: pg_stat_activity and p99 write latency dashboard.
- Force read-only to protect data:
  kubectl -n payments set env deploy/payments-api READ_ONLY_MODE=true
- Trigger failover via Patroni (coordinate with DB on-call @marco.lee).
- After primary is healthy, revert READ_ONLY_MODE and run migrations if needed.

Operational Commands
- Pods and health:
  kubectl -n payments get pods -o wide
  kubectl -n payments describe deploy/payments-api
- Logs (last 5 min, errors):
  kubectl -n payments logs deploy/payments-api --since=5m | grep -i "error"
- Feature flags (inspect):
  curl -s http://flagr.flagr:18000/api/v1/flags | jq '.[] | select(.key | test("payments"))'

Rollback
- To previous stable deployment (recorded in release notes):
  kubectl -n payments rollout undo deploy/payments-api --to-revision=stable
  kubectl -n payments rollout status deploy/payments-api --timeout=5m

Escalation
- Primary: Payments on-call (PagerDuty)
- Secondary: @marco.lee (SRE), @anita.shah (Payments EM)
- Compliance/SOX approval: @compliance.ops during business hours

Post-Incident Actions
- Create Jira: PAY-INC templated ticket; attach Grafana snapshots and Sentry issues.
- Update Statuspage with RCA within 48 hours.
- Run replay job if needed:
  kubectl -n payments create job --from=cronjob/payments-replay replay-$(date +%s)

Related Docs
- Architecture: Confluence → Payments → Architecture Overview (ID 66290431)
- Error Budget Policy: Confluence → SRE → SLOs (ID 55321098)

Change Log
- 2025-08-22 (v2): Updated 3DS outage steps, added Kafka lag scaling guidance, clarified rollback, refreshed escalation contacts.

# 2025-03-14 API Latency Spike (INC-2387)
## Summary
From 09:12–09:58 UTC, P95 latency for /v1/orders increased from 320 ms to 2.8 s, causing timeouts for ~7.6% of requests in us-east-1.
## Impact
- Affected services: orders-api, payment-orchestrator
- Customers impacted: ~14% of marketplace checkouts in NA; 53 support tickets
- Revenue at risk: $82k; no data loss reported.
## Timeline
- 09:12 UTC: PagerDuty alert "Latencies > 1.5s" fired (SRE on-call: J. Ortega).
- 09:18 UTC: Identified correlation with orders-api v2025.03.14 rollout.
- 09:24 UTC: Mitigated by rolling back orders-api to v2025.03.12-rc3.
- 09:58 UTC: Latencies normalized; incident resolved.
## Root Cause
A change in Redis connection pool settings (maxIdle=100 -> 10) in orders-api v2025.03.14 introduced severe connection churn under burst load; see diff https://git.example.com/commerce/orders-api/-/merge_requests/1427.
## Remediation
- [x] Reverted config to previous defaults and added alert on Redis pool saturation (PLAT-9123).
- [ ] Add load-test scenario for bursty checkout patterns in CI (QA-774).
- [ ] Guardrails: block config reductions >50% without perf sign-off (SRE-215).
## References
- Incident: https://jira.example.com/browse/INC-2387
- Dashboard: https://grafana.example.com/d/latency/orders
- Runbook: https://confluence.example.com/display/ENG/Orders+API+Runbook

Create a public gist named git-prune-merged.sh with the description "Safely prune local Git branches already merged into origin/main; prompts before deletion and skips main/master/develop/current branch" containing the following Bash script as its content: 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Prune local branches that have been merged into origin/main, skipping protected branches and prompting before deletion.
BASE=${1:-origin/main}

git fetch --prune
current=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
protected=("main" "master" "develop" "$current")

mapfile -t merged < <(git branch --format="%(refname:short)" --merged "$BASE" | sed 's/* //')

to_delete=()
for br in "${merged[@]}"; do
  skip=false
  for pb in "${protected[@]}"; do
    if [[ "$br" == "$pb" ]]; then
      skip=true; break
    fi
  done
  if [[ "$br" != "$BASE" && "$skip" == false ]]; then
    to_delete+=("$br")
  fi
done

if (( ${#to_delete[@]} == 0 )); then
  echo "No local branches to delete."
  exit 0
fi

printf "Branches to delete (%d):\n" "${#to_delete[@]}"
printf ' - %s\n' "${to_delete[@]}"

read -p "Proceed with deletion? [y/N] " ans
if [[ "$ans" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
  for br in "${to_delete[@]}"; do
    git branch -d "$br" || git branch -D "$br"
  done
  echo "Done."
else
  echo "Aborted."
fi

Create a public gist with the description “Git post-merge hook to auto-install dependencies when package manifests change” and filename “post-merge.sh”, containing this Bash script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Git post-merge hook: auto-install deps if package manifests changed
set -euo pipefail

# If no previous HEAD is available (e.g., initial clone), exit quietly
if ! git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD@{1} >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  exit 0
fi

changed_files="$(git diff --name-only HEAD@{1} HEAD || true)"
pattern='(^|/)(package\.json|package-lock\.json|yarn\.lock|pnpm-lock\.yaml)$'

if echo "$changed_files" | grep -Eq "$pattern"; then
  if command -v pnpm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[post-merge] Detected dependency changes; running pnpm install..."
    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile || pnpm install
  elif command -v yarn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[post-merge] Detected dependency changes; running yarn install..."
    yarn install --frozen-lockfile || yarn install
  else
    echo "[post-merge] Detected dependency changes; running npm ci (fallback to npm install)..."
    npm ci || npm install
  fi
else
  echo "[post-merge] No dependency manifest changes detected."
fi
